processing: A green tea made in flat and needle shapes from a local large-leaf cultivar, fixed, shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Early: buds stir in late February and picking usually starts in early March.
appearance_dry: Tender green and downy, either flat and even or tight, fine and straight.
taste_profile: Mellow, full and clean, with a strong chestnut aroma and a downy note.

brewing.notes: General green-tea advice: this is a fuller leaf than most tender bud teas and takes slightly hotter water, but long steeps still turn it sharp.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year spring green, as usual for its class. It reaches market unusually early, from early March, so the first lots of the year appear well before many other Chinese greens.
description:
Nanjiang Dayecha is both a plant and a tea: a local large-leaf cultivar from Nanjiang County, in the Micang Mountains of northern Sichuan, and the protected green tea made from it. That makes it unusual, since most Chinese greens lean on small-leaf bushes.

The bush buds early, grows sturdy shoots and keeps them tender for a while, which is why researchers singled it out for quality green tea. Producers shape it either flat or into fine needles, and the shape tells you which style you have.

In the cup it is a bright tender green with a chestnut and downy aroma and a fuller body than the leaf size might lead you to fear; it is mellow rather than harsh. Slightly hotter water than for a delicate bud tea helps, as long as you keep the steeps short.

Good lots come from the zone between about 800 and 1,200 metres. Look for spring tea and the protected name, and try a flat and a needle side by side if you can.
history:
The cultivar was first found in 1958 at Mudanyuan in Jintai village, Liuba township, and its growing area was surveyed in 1961. In February 1965 it was recognised as one of 21 national local fine varieties.

In 1987 the county's tea institute set up a seed-stock farm at Huangcaoping, and six selections followed, among them Nanjiang No. 2, later approved as a national variety. The Ministry of Agriculture registered the name as an agricultural geographical indication on 27 November 2009.
